newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia says launches digital receiver.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says launches digital receiver.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy said in a statement on Wednesday it had launched a digital satellite receiver with a common interface, enabling end-users to receive services from many TV-programme providers.

The common interface comes with "a standardised interface as a solution to the many problems synonymous with the uptake of digital TV transmissions and is supported by many broadcasters including public service companies," Nokia said.
End-users would benefit from a universal digital receiver that will enable reception of services from a number of programme providers, it said.
"The launch follows Nokia's agreement with Telenor Satellite Services for development, manufacturing and marketing of common interface-based digital receivers (IRD).
No world-wide standard exists for the encryption format, or conditional access, of digital TV-broadcasts ensuring that transmissions reach only entitled viewers, Nokia noted.

"The common interface standardised CA (conditional access) modules can be inserted into the IRDs and the end-user will be happy with one digital receiver," it said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, news@reuters.fi
